title: Brevard County School Board, District 2
what_it_does: School board members set the district budget and school-tax rate, hire the superintendent (where appointed), approve school boundaries, curriculum policy and construction, and set district policies. Nonpartisan.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); both candidates are marked Qualified, which for a nonpartisan seat means the August vote did not produce a majority winner (or the seat is decided only in November). Positions have not been researched; check the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.name: Kyle Savage
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: U.S. Army veteran (military police); former elementary school teacher
candidates.background: Kyle Savage served in the U.S. Army as a military police officer, including protective security work for senior commanders. He holds a Florida K-6 teaching certificate and taught fifth- and sixth-grade math and science at Cape View Elementary School in Cape Canaveral. He is a father of three and finished second in the August 2026 primary with about 31% of the vote.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

school_books.summary: Savage opposed the board's attempt to remove about 298 books in a single motion and says each challenge should be reviewed individually by a committee that includes both parents and educators, with no blanket bans.
school_books.quote: I want a clear, consistent process: individual challenges reviewed on their own merits by a real committee with parent and educator input

sources.title: 2026 Voter's Guide - Brevard County School Board District 2
Brevard County School Board District 2 overview

teacher_pay.summary: Savage says Brevard teachers are paid more than $2,500 below the state average and pledges to make compensation a priority in every budget cycle.
teacher_pay.quote: Brevard teachers are paid more than $2,500 below the state average

sources.title: 2026 Voter's Guide - Brevard County School Board District 2

school_safety.summary: Savage would put a school resource officer in every school and two in larger schools, and also calls for consistent discipline policy and mental-health resources, saying safety depends on trained people, clear protocols and no gaps.
school_safety.quote: Safety isn't a slogan; it's showing up every day for the basics.

sources.title: Brevard County School Board District 2 overview
2026 Voter's Guide - Brevard County School Board District 2

taxes.summary: Rather than further cuts, Savage proposes growing enrollment and revenue by expanding VPK to every elementary school, building a vocational-technical center and moving district staff into underused buildings instead of closing schools. He also wants a plain-language budget breakdown published every year.

candidates.name: Gene Trent
candidates.occupation: Brevard County School Board member, District 2; former classroom teacher
candidates.background: Gene Trent was elected to the Brevard County School Board's District 2 seat in 2022 and served as board vice chair. He describes more than 20 years as a classroom educator. He led the August 2026 primary with about 42% of the vote and faces Kyle Savage in the November runoff.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

school_books.summary: As board vice chair in November 2023 Trent moved, without the item being on the agenda, to remove about 298 books from Brevard classrooms and libraries based on a state list of titles pulled in other districts, bypassing individual review. The motion failed 3-2 and Trent said he would bring it back.
school_books.quote: We need to move forward. We owe it to the public.

sources.title: Brevard school board shoots down Trent's motion to use state list as guide to ban books

taxes.summary: In an August 2025 video Trent questioned whether the district needed about $7 million in federal funding, saying money alone does not solve problems, and has described cutting open positions and returning resource teachers to classrooms as his budget approach.
taxes.quote: Maybe we don't need that money... throwing money at an issue doesn't solve it.

sources.title: Brevard County School Board District 2 overview

school_safety.summary: Trent has supported metal detectors in schools and expansion of the Guardian Program, which arms and trains designated school staff to respond to threats.

sources.title: Brevard County School Board District 2 overview

other_issues.title: Teacher pay and retention
other_issues.summary: Trent's campaign site lists 'competitive pay, professional growth' among his priorities and claims improved teacher retention as a result of his term. He did not return the 2026 voter-guide questionnaire.
